readmeExcerpt: # AI Agent Deep Dive **English** | [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md) ## Quick Links PDF reports: - New: **Hermes Agent Source Code Deep Dive** - Claude Code: [ai-agent-deep-dive-v2.1.pdf](./ai-agent-deep-dive-v2.1.pdf), including the new Chapter 8: Memory System. - Claude Code: [ai-agent-deep-dive-v2.pdf](./ai-agent-deep-dive-v2.pdf). ## Educational Agent Code This repository also includes a **minimal Python agent built for learning**, demonstrating how to structure the core components of an AI agent. ### Where to Find the Code - Agent core: [`src/agt/agent.py`](./src/agt/agent.py) - CLI entry point: [`src/agt/cli.py`](./src/agt/cli.py) - Learning materials: [`docs/`](./docs) ### Project Goals This minimal agent is designed for educational use, with an emphasis on: - Keeping the structure clear. - Avoiding unnecessary engineering complexity. - Keeping the core code small and easy to explore. - Focusing on the agent loop, a Fake LLM interface, skill discovery, and the CLI skeleton. ### Running the Minimal Agent The project uses Poetry to manage dependencies. #### 1. Install Dependencies ```bash poetry install ``` #### 2. Run the Agent CLI ```bash poetry run agt "Hello" ``` #### 3. List Available Skills ```bash poetry run agt --skills-dir ./skills --list-skills ``` ### Current Implementation The current version is a **minimal educational implementation**. It does not yet connect to a real remote model API. It includes a replaceable Fake LLM that returns a test response in streamed text chunks for each user input. This keeps the model integration separate from the agent itself: connecting a real model later only requires replacing the LLM call layer, rather than rewriting the agent.
readmeHtml:
AI Agent Deep Dive

English | 简体中文

Quick Links

PDF reports:

  • New: Hermes Agent Source Code Deep Dive
  • Claude Code: ai-agent-deep-dive-v2.1.pdf, including the new Chapter 8: Memory System.
  • Claude Code: ai-agent-deep-dive-v2.pdf.

Educational Agent Code

This repository also includes a minimal Python agent built for learning, demonstrating how to structure the core components of an AI agent.

Where to Find the Code

  • Agent core: src/agt/agent.py
  • CLI entry point: src/agt/cli.py
  • Learning materials: docs/

Project Goals

This minimal agent is designed for educational use, with an emphasis on:

  • Keeping the structure clear.
  • Avoiding unnecessary engineering complexity.
  • Keeping the core code small and easy to explore.
  • Focusing on the agent loop, a Fake LLM interface, skill discovery, and the CLI skeleton.

Running the Minimal Agent

The project uses Poetry to manage dependencies.

1. Install Dependencies

poetry install

2. Run the Agent CLI

poetry run agt "Hello"

3. List Available Skills

poetry run agt --skills-dir ./skills --list-skills

Current Implementation

The current version is a minimal educational implementation. It does not yet connect to a real remote model API.

It includes a replaceable Fake LLM that returns a test response in streamed text chunks for each user input.

This keeps the model integration separate from the agent itself: connecting a real model later only requires replacing the LLM call layer, rather than rewriting the agent.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An in-depth research report and source code analysis of various AI agent architectures.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: AI Agent Deep Dive is a comprehensive research repository dedicated to the detailed source code and architectural analysis of modern AI agent frameworks. It serves as an in-depth educational resource, breaking down how complex systems implement core agent functionalities like memory management, tool usage, planning, and execution loops. The project demystifies abstract agent concepts by providing meticulous technical teardowns and structural breakdowns of popular open-source codebases. In addition to PDF reports, it includes a minimal, teaching-focused Python agent project to practically demonstrate how core agent loops and skills should be organized.
keyFeatures: Source Code Analysis: Provides detailed, code-level teardowns of popular open-source AI agent repositories and architectures.
Architecture Comparison: Contrasts the design choices, memory systems, and execution loops of different leading agent frameworks.
Technical Documentation: Offers deep insights via PDF reports into how theoretical concepts like RAG and planning are implemented in reality.
Minimal Teaching Agent: Includes a stripped-down, structural Python agent project specifically designed for educational demonstration.
Centralized Research: Acts as a single, curated point of reference for developers studying agent implementations and industry trends.
